text:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and another computer on the internet, and everything you send goes through it scrambled.

Normally, websites see your own internet address, and your internet provider can see which sites you visit. With a VPN, your device locks (encrypts) your data and sends it to the VPN company's computer first. That computer unlocks it and talks to the website for you.

So:

The website sees the VPN's address, not yours.
Your internet provider sees only scrambled data going to the VPN.
On public Wi-Fi, strangers can't read what you send.

A VPN doesn't make you fully anonymous, since the VPN company can still see your activity. It also won't protect you from viruses or fake websites.
